# The Frozen Wastes · Book II, pp. 172–177
# Generated by the extractor — fix the extractor, not this file.
PAGE	172
P	North of the <b>Whitefang Mountains</b> (page 480) lies a vast steppe, a windswept sea of shortgrass, sedge, and lichen. No trees grow here. The landscape is broken only by rocky outcrops, low moraines, and kettle lakes. It rarely snows and almost never rains, but hail is somewhat common.
P	Caribou and mammoths graze the plateau, preyed on by wolves and saber-toothed cats and terrible things that crawl forth from the lakes in summer. Bands of mammoth herders roam in warmer months. But for the most part, it's an empty and forlorn place.
H2	Impressions
HR
H3	Always
B	A landscape so wide and empty you can see the horizon curve
B	The constant wind, whispering and howling, tugging and lashing
B	Patterns forming in the windswept grass or snow, or the growth of flowers, like runes that fade just before you can read them
B	The swell of anger, the urge to inflict violence on your companions, as your temper and patience fray
HR
ICON	icons/spring.svg
H3	Spring
B	Yellow and brown grass, splashed with pale violet flowers
B	Fields of standing water, just inches deep, reflecting the empty sky
B	Squelch and crackle of half-frozen soil underfoot Farther north, the plateau gets even colder, even windier, the steppe giving way to tundra. Eventually, a mountain-like wall of <b>dark ice</b> (page 322) blocks the way, stretching across the horizon. The glacier is the final working of the <b>Rime Lords</b> (page 316). It seals a rift in the world, and keeps the worst of the <b>Howling Curse</b> (page 492) at bay. Mammoth herders come here to quarry dark ice, slowly chipping the glacier away.
ICON	icons/summer.svg
H3	Summer
B	Days that last forever, the sun never truly setting
B	Mix of bright green grass, red lichen, white flowers
B	Swarms of insects, spawned from muddy soil
B	Birds and <b>ice drakes</b> (page 491) pecking at the soil or flocking to the sky

B	Long shadows in the low, low sun
B	Sharp cold edge to the wind
B	The restless foraging of small animals

H3	Winter
B	Endless night, the sun barely rising at noon
B	Thin carpet of frost and snow, shrubs and dead grass poking out
B	The ceaseless, gnawing wind and cold
B	The sense that you've made a terrible mistake in coming here

H2	Traversing the Wastes
HR
P	The Frozen Wastes are inhospitable in a way that southerners can barely comprehend. On any expedition into the wastes:
C	You need a knowledgeable guide, like a <b>mammoth herder</b> (page 177), who knows the ways of this place
C	You need lots of firewood or dried dung, for you'll find no fuel and even in the summer the "nights" can be freezing
C	The way will be grueling (from cold and mud and bugs); you risk exhausting yourselves/your supplies
C	You need to watch out for predators, like <b>wolves</b> (page 209) or mchebra-gris (<b>kleztigrs</b>, basically, see page 379)
C	You need to watch out for kettle lakes, easily mistaken for ice or shallow standing water
C	You risk succumbing to the <b>Howling</b> <b>Curse</b> (page 492), which taints much of the Wastes
H2	Questions
Q	What precious flower grows only in the Frozen Wastes, blooming for a few days each summer? Why is it so valuable?
Q	What do you find most surprising about this place?
Q	What do you find yourself missing the most, out here in vast and empty space?
Q	What is ___ doing, that you find so damned annoying?
Q	If you had to kill ___, how would you do it?
Q	If it came down to it, which of your companions would you eat first?
H2	Hooks
HR
B	A villain that the PCs want dead flees north, into the Frozen Wastes
B	Only one thing can kill the <b>Crombil</b> (page 62), and it lies at the bottom of a kettle lake
B	The dark ice glacier that contains the <b>Howling Curse</b> (page 492) has begun to melt and recede

H2	Mammoth herders
HR
P	Here's a typical band:
P	<b>Size</b> <i>hamlet</i> (~15-30 souls)
P	<b>Population</b> +0
P	<b>Prosperity</b> -1
B	Trade with (pick 1 or 2)...
E	other mammoth herders
E	a farming valley
E	a fortress-monastery
P	<b>Resources</b>
B	Mammoths (wool, ivory, bone, dung)
B	Sleds/sledges of bone, hide, timber
B	Hunting (wild mammoths, caribou, hare, fish)
B	Gathering (timber, ivory, bone, flint, herbs, <b>dark ice</b> (page 322) <b>Defenses</b> +0
B	Mammoth-mounted warriors
B	Hounds and hunting drakes
B	Spears/javelins tipped with dark ice, flint, bone, or bronze (<i>crude</i>)
P	About half of each band are youngsters, with the rest being able-bodied adults.
P	Elders rarely allow themselves to survive long enough to become a burden to the others. A band typically keeps a herd of 10 to 20 adult <b>mammoths</b> (page 177), plus a few young. They butcher their own beasts only when desperate, keeping them instead for wool, transport, and labor.
P	A band spends the warmer months on the Frozen Wastes, but spend the colder months sheltering in the caves, ruins, and forests of the <b>Whitefang Mountains</b> (page 480). They'll trade with <b>valley farms</b> (page 484) or <b>fortress-monasteries</b> (page 486) in spring, before heading out into the Wastes, or in autumn, before they encamp for the winter.
P	<b>Something interesting:</b> Mammoth herders tend to be impeccably polite, with drawn-out, formal greetings and elaborate, almost artistic ways of doing everything from lacing up a parka to butchering a beast.
P	<b>Something useful:</b> These rituals help identify those afflicted with the <b>Howling</b> <b>Curse</b> (page 492), who lack in patience and good grace. Alas, this means that mammoth herders interpret frustration or bad manners as a sign of being accursed.
H2	Names
HR
P	Tibetan-inspired: Bhokhi, Cheyez, Dangyi, Gamyang, Lhing, Jongash, Nayan, Ningo, Nyayelar, Paing, Ramang, Samanz, Sewas, Tawaro, Tsaru, Tsetse, Wasen, Yenphi

H2	Trade & Barter
HR
H3	Commonly available
P	The following are special items in Stonetop, but commonly available among mammoth herders—if the PCs are on friendly terms with a band, they can acquire these items without having to roll. They do need to trade something of equal Value. Food, iron, glass, and wool are usually in demand.
P	They have little to no use for finery.
VT	goods
VR	Ivory a bit (comb, pendant, etc.)	0*
VR	◇ a substantial piece	1*
VR	a mammoth tusk (immobile)	2*
VR	cartload of mammoth tusks	3*
VR	Dark ice (magical, see page 322) a small piece (magical)	1
VR	◇ a large chunk (magical)	2
VR	with special characteristics	+1
VR	a functional tool or weapon	+2
VF	* +1 if sold/traded on to anyone other than mammoth herders
VT	livestock
VR	Hound, follower (keen-nosed, fierce, tireless); HP 6; Damage d6 (hand, grabby); Instinct to chase; Cost a full belly	1
VR	Hunting drake, follower (tiny, sharp- eyed, swift-winged); HP 3; Damage d4 (hand); Instinct to test its limits; Cost hours/days of training	1
VR	Mammoth (huge, hardy, keen-nosed); HP 15; Damage d6+5 (reach, forceful, or hand, area, forceful); Instinct to suffer no insult or threat; sickly in warmer climes	3

H2	Dangers
HR
H3	Hazards
B	Brutal cold and ceaseless wind, leading to <b>hypothermia & frostbite</b> (page 489)
B	Hail storms—annoying, pelting (d4 damage), smashing (d6 damage)
B	Mud—sucking, cold, exhausting
B	Slippery footing
B	Still, reflective water hiding a sudden, plunging drop into a kettle
B	In summer: swarms of midges/ mosquitos—annoying, distracting, painful, diseased
B	Getting lost or misjudging time in the vast featureless terrain
B	<b>Whispers and visions</b> (page 428), pushing people towards bloodshed, cruelty, and savagery
B	Places tainted by the <b>Howling Curse</b> (page 492)
H3	Monsters
B	<b>Ice drakes</b> (page 491), especially in warmer months
B	<b>Kleztigrs</b> (page 379), called "mchebragris" in the local tongue
B	<b>Wolves</b> (page 209)
B	A <b>frythanc</b> (page 133), nesting in the Whitefangs and preying on caribou or even mammoths
B	<b>Wraiths</b> (page 79) of those who died of starvation and want, or corrupted by the <b>Howling Curse</b> (page 492)
B	<b>Spirits of the wild</b> (page 356)
B	<b>Tulpas</b> (page 324), free-roaming or bound to something nearby
B	<b>Kyakaara</b> (page 493), perhaps what remains of a corrupted band of mammoth herders

H3	Mammoth herder
P	<i>Horde</i>, <i>hardy</i>, <i>cautious</i>, <i>organized</i>, <i>clever</i>
P	<b>HP</b> 7; <b>Armor</b> 1 (thick hides & furs)

P	<b>Instinct</b> to put their people and their herd first
P	• Greet someone from a distance, politely and formally
P	• Remain calm as they prepare for violence
P	• Work or fight in tandem with their mammoth(s), dogs, and hunting drakes
